cards.text: Jesus has been raised from the dead, and later, by the Sea of Tiberias, He shows Himself to His disciples again. Seven of them are together: Simon Peter, Thomas called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana in Galilee, two other disciples, and the sons of Zebedee, James and John (Matthew 4:21).

cards.question: The disciples are together by the sea. Simon Peter tells the others what he's going to do. What is it?
The others tell Peter they'll go with him. They get into the boat and stay out all night, and by morning they've caught ___.

cards.text: After a whole night of nothing, early in the morning Jesus is standing on the shore, but the disciples don't recognize that it's Him. I've stared at dough that wouldn't rise till the sun came up, friend, so believe me, I FEEL that boat.

cards.question: The disciples don't know it's Jesus on the shore. He calls out to them in the boat. What does He ask?

answers.text: If He can use their boat

cards.question: The disciples tell the Man on the shore they have no fish. He tells them to cast the net on the right side of the boat, and He says they will find some.
The disciples cast the net right where the Man on the shore says. What happens when they try to haul it in?

answers.text: They can't with so many fish

cards.question: The net is too full to haul in. Then the disciple whom Jesus loved turns to Peter and says, "It is the ___!"
As soon as Simon Peter hears that the Man on the shore is the Lord, he stays put in the boat to help with the net.

cards.text: Peter puts his outer garment back on, since he'd taken it off, and jumps into the sea. The man got DRESSED to go swimming, and friend, I respect it.

cards.question: Peter's in the water. The other disciples come ashore in the boat, dragging the net full of fish. They're more than a mile from land.

cards.text: When they land, there's a charcoal fire there with fish on it, and some bread. That's like dragging yourself into the bakery before sunrise and the oven's already warm, a batch already cooling, and you didn't do a THING.

cards.question: Jesus already has fish on the fire, so He tells the disciples there's no need to bring any of their catch.
Simon Peter goes aboard and drags the net ashore. It's full of large fish. How many?
Peter drags the net ashore with 153 large fish in it, but even with so many, the net is not ___.

cards.text: “Come, have breakfast,” Jesus says to them. Not one disciple dares to ask Him who He is, and they all know it's the Lord.

cards.question: Breakfast by the fire is ready. Who comes and hands the bread and the fish to the disciples?
This breakfast by the sea was now the ___ time that Jesus appeared to the disciples after He was raised from the dead.

cards.text: John's not done telling this one, friend. Keep your apron on.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 1 mentions jam, a food that isn't a cookie and isn't in the passage.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 8 quotes "It is the ___!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess the exact word in the beloved disciple's line ("It is the ___!"). Card 4 already told the baker the man is Jesus, so this tests the wording, not the meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Teacher" means nearly the same as "Lord" here, since both identify Jesus. A baker could argue it's right.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: "The disciple whom Jesus loved" is much longer than "Jesus Himself" and "Simon Peter", so the answers aren't about the same length.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: "John's not done telling this one" presents John as the writer of this Gospel. The passage never names its writer, and no reference is given. Card 1 also names John as a son of Zebedee, which ties the two together. The docs allow outside facts like who wrote a letter "with their reference", but this Gospel's authorship has no verse that states it.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin name John as the writer of the Gospel of John when no verse names him, or should continuation lines avoid naming the Gospel's writer?

findings.problem: This card is only the story-continues line and tells nothing from John 21:14, but it cites John 21:14. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, no wider and no narrower. The docs allow a card that is just this line but don't say what it cites.
findings.question: What should the "verses" field be on a final story card that is only the story-continues line and tells no verse?
